posts.headline:
Paper notes work.
Until they don't.
posts.body: When records live in notebooks, photos and messages, the dog's full history gets harder to follow.
posts.footer: Built for calmer canine therapy admin
posts.caption:
Paper notes can be useful in the moment.

The problem starts when the full picture is spread across notebooks, phone photos, WhatsApp messages and memory.

Wolds Record is being built to help canine therapists keep each dog's record history clear, calm and easy to return to.
posts.altText: Wolds Record square Instagram graphic about paper notes becoming hard to manage for canine therapy records.

posts.headline:
Vet-ready reports
shouldn't take all evening.
posts.body: Session notes should already contain the structure you need for professional, useful reports.
posts.caption:
Writing a vet report should not mean rebuilding the record history from scratch.

If the right details are captured during each session, reporting becomes a calmer final step rather than another admin mountain.

That is one of the workflows Wolds Record is being built around.
posts.altText: Wolds Record square Instagram graphic about making vet-ready reports easier for canine therapists.

posts.headline:
Canine therapists
deserve canine-first software.
posts.body: Not generic notes. Not horse-first systems. A quieter tool shaped around dogs and the people treating them.
posts.footer: Wolds Record is being built for this niche
posts.caption:
Canine therapists do specialist work.

Their software should understand that context instead of forcing them into generic workflows or systems designed for a different industry.

Wolds Record is being built specifically around canine therapy records, record histories and reporting.
posts.altText: Wolds Record square Instagram graphic saying canine therapists deserve canine-first software.

posts.headline: Built around a real therapy workflow.
posts.body: From first enquiry to session notes and reports, the product is being shaped around how canine therapists actually work.
posts.footer: Practical software for practical treatment work
posts.caption:
Wolds Record is not being designed from a generic admin checklist.

It is being shaped around real canine therapy workflows: dogs, owners, sessions, progress, aftercare and reports.

The aim is simple: make the admin feel calmer without losing the important clinical context.
posts.altText: Wolds Record square graphic about building software around a real canine therapy workflow.

posts.headline: A dog profile should remember the useful things.
posts.body: Owner details, vet context, cautions, goals and the notes you need before the next session.
posts.footer: Everything starts with the dog record
posts.caption:
A good dog profile is more than a name and a phone number.

It should help you quickly understand the dog's background, the owner's priorities, the current plan and what matters before the next appointment.

That is the kind of record Wolds Record is being built to support.
posts.altText: Wolds Record square graphic about useful dog profile records for canine therapists.

posts.headline:
Progress is hard to spot
when notes are scattered.
posts.body: Small changes matter. They are easier to see when each session builds on the last.
posts.caption:
Progress in canine therapy can be subtle.

A change in comfort, confidence, movement or owner feedback might only make sense when you can see the thread over several sessions.

Wolds Record is being built to make that thread easier to follow.
posts.altText: Wolds Record square graphic about tracking progress across canine therapy sessions.

posts.headline: Owner context belongs with the record.
posts.body: Questions, concerns, aftercare notes and consent details should be easy to find when you need them.
posts.footer: Keep the admin close to the work
posts.caption:
Canine therapy is not just treatment notes.

Owner questions, consent, home observations and aftercare conversations all form part of the picture.

Wolds Record is being built to keep that useful context connected to the dog's record.
posts.altText: Wolds Record square graphic about keeping owner context with canine therapy record records.

posts.headline:
Aftercare notes
should be easy to revisit.
posts.body: What you advised last time should be simple to check before the next conversation.
posts.caption:
Aftercare advice is part of the treatment story.

When it is easy to revisit what was discussed last time, follow-up conversations become clearer and more consistent.

That is the kind of admin Wolds Record is designed to make less fragile.
posts.altText: Wolds Record square graphic about revisiting aftercare notes for canine therapy clients.

posts.headline:
Before the next session,
you need the story so far.
posts.body: The last note, current goals and owner feedback should be ready before the dog arrives.
posts.footer: A calmer way to pick up the record
posts.caption:
Before a dog comes back in, you need the useful picture quickly.

What happened last time? What changed at home? What are you watching for today?

Wolds Record is being built so therapists can pick up the thread without digging through scattered notes.
posts.altText: Wolds Record square graphic about reviewing the story so far before a canine therapy session.

posts.headline: Clear records make vet communication easier.
posts.body: When the record history is organised, professional updates take less time to prepare.
posts.caption:
Good communication starts with good records.

When session notes, observations and progress are organised, it is easier to prepare a professional update for a vet or referral partner.

Wolds Record is being built to support that standard.
posts.altText: Wolds Record square graphic about clear records supporting vet communication.

posts.headline:
Solo practitioners
carry the whole admin load.
posts.body: Appointments, notes, clients, follow-ups and reports often sit on one person's shoulders.
posts.caption:
Many canine therapists are doing brilliant work while carrying all the admin themselves.

Appointments, notes, reports, follow-ups and owner communication can quickly become a lot for one person.

Wolds Record is being built with that reality in mind.
posts.altText: Wolds Record square graphic about solo practitioners carrying the whole admin load.

posts.headline:
Calm software
beats complicated software.
posts.body: Therapists need clear workflows, not another system that takes hours to manage.
posts.caption:
The goal is not to build software that feels clever.

The goal is to build software that feels calm, clear and useful in the middle of a real working week.

That is the design standard for Wolds Record.
posts.altText: Wolds Record square graphic saying calm software beats complicated software.

posts.headline: A session note should do more than tick a box.
posts.body: It should capture what changed, what mattered and what needs checking next time.
posts.caption:
A session note is not just admin.

It can capture what changed, what the owner noticed, what was treated, how the dog responded and what should be checked next time.

Wolds Record is being built to make that easier to capture consistently.
posts.altText: Wolds Record square graphic about session notes doing more than ticking a box.

posts.headline: Every feature has to earn its place.
posts.body: If it does not help a therapist record, review or report more clearly, it waits.
posts.caption:
We are trying to be careful about what goes into Wolds Record.

Every feature has to earn its place by making record keeping, review or reporting clearer for canine therapists.

Useful before clever. Calm before crowded.
posts.altText: Wolds Record square graphic about product features earning their place.

posts.headline: Your workflow can help shape this.
posts.body: We want feedback from canine therapists who know the admin pain points first-hand.
posts.footer: Tell us what would save you time
posts.caption:
Wolds Record is still being shaped.

If you are a canine therapist, your workflow, frustrations and reporting habits are exactly the kind of feedback that can make this product better.

What admin task would you most like to make easier?
posts.altText: Wolds Record square graphic inviting canine therapists to share workflow feedback.

posts.headline:
Professional records
help build professional trust.
posts.body: Clear notes make it easier to explain decisions, share progress and show the care behind the work.
posts.caption:
Professional records are not just for compliance.

They help show the thinking behind your work, the progress over time and the care taken with each dog.

Wolds Record is being built to make that professionalism easier to maintain.
posts.altText: Wolds Record square graphic about professional records helping build trust.

posts.headline: Client questions are easier with the record history close.
posts.body: When the notes are organised, answers can be calmer, clearer and more consistent.
posts.caption:
Clients often ask good questions between sessions.

When the record history is close to hand, it is easier to answer calmly and consistently without searching through old messages or trying to remember every detail.

That is one reason organised records matter.
posts.altText: Wolds Record square graphic about answering client questions with organised record history.

posts.headline:
Spreadsheets can track data.
They don't manage the whole record.
posts.body: Dogs, owners, sessions, reports and aftercare need to connect in a way that feels natural.
posts.caption:
Spreadsheets are useful for some things.

But canine therapy records are more than rows and columns. They involve dogs, owners, history, sessions, observations, follow-ups and reports.

Wolds Record is being built to connect that context more naturally.
posts.altText: Wolds Record square graphic about spreadsheets not managing the whole canine therapy record.

posts.headline:
Follow-up starts
with what you recorded last time.
posts.body: The next appointment is easier when your previous note tells you what to check, ask and compare.
posts.caption:
Good follow-up depends on good notes.

The previous session should help you know what to ask, what to compare and what to watch for next time.

Wolds Record is being built around that practical rhythm.
posts.altText: Wolds Record square graphic about follow-up starting with the previous session note.

posts.headline: Want to help shape Wolds Record?
posts.body: We are looking for canine therapists who can tell us what record keeping really needs to do.
posts.footer: Follow along or send us a message
posts.caption:
We are building Wolds Record for canine therapists, so feedback from canine therapists matters most.

If you have strong opinions about session notes, reports, record histories or admin pain points, we would love to hear them.

Follow along or send us a message.
posts.altText: Wolds Record square graphic asking canine therapists to help shape the product.
